stories.headline: Deal with US not imminent, Iran says
stories.summary: Iran's government contradicts market expectations by stating that a negotiated agreement with the United States remains distant, even as diplomatic discussions show incremental movement. The statement tempers recent optimism that had driven down oil prices on speculation that a deal could soon ease sanctions and increase global energy supplies.

stories.headline: How did a rare strain of Ebola outrun doctors?
stories.summary: A rare Ebola strain spreads rapidly across the Democratic Republic of Congo and into Uganda, with confirmed cases now exceeding 900 and suspected deaths reaching 220. Health workers struggle to contain the outbreak due to insecurity, resource shortages, and the virus's speed of transmission outpacing their response capacity.

stories.headline: Pope Leo Warns of Risks From A.I. in 42,300-Word Encyclical
stories.summary: Pope Leo has released a lengthy encyclical examining artificial intelligence's dangers, calling for the technology to be constrained and redesigned to serve human dignity rather than corporate or military interests. The papal document positions AI regulation as a moral imperative, arguing that uncontrolled technological advancement threatens fundamental human values and social stability.

stories.headline: Israel kills three in attacks on Lebanon, issues more displacement orders
stories.summary: Israel conducts attacks that kill three people in Lebanon and orders additional civilian evacuations from villages in the border region. Lebanese leadership maintains that complete Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory remains a core demand, even as some Israeli officials push for renewed military operations despite ongoing diplomatic discussions.

stories.headline: First Hong Kong astronaut launches into space onboard Chinese mission
stories.summary: Hong Kong astronaut Lai Ka-ying launches aboard China's Shenzhou 23 spacecraft, marking the first time someone from Hong Kong has traveled to space. One of the three crew members will remain on China's space station for approximately a year as part of Beijing's continued expansion of its orbital capabilities and lunar exploration program.

stories.headline: Timelapse shows Hajj pilgrims performing Tawaf in Mecca
stories.summary: Millions of Muslim pilgrims have gathered in Mecca to perform Tawaf, the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba that forms a central part of the annual Hajj pilgrimage. This year's gathering takes place amid regional tensions and extreme heat, yet participants continue the centuries-old spiritual practice that draws believers from across the world.

stories.headline: Surf photographer attacked in water by 'shark or sea lion'
stories.summary: A photographer was injured in the water during a surfing competition in New Zealand, with the attacking animal remaining unidentified as either a shark or sea lion. Event organizers issued a code red warning and halted the contest as a precaution while authorities investigated the incident.

stories.headline: Greek swimmer only athlete to beat world record at controversial Enhanced Games
stories.summary: Greek swimmer Ioannis Gkolomeev sets a new record in the 50-meter freestyle at the Enhanced Games, an experimental competition that permits performance-enhancing drugs. Despite the relaxed restrictions, most athletes at the event fail to surpass existing world records, making Gkolomeev's achievement a notable exception.

stories.headline: Clashes as Venezuelan prisoners protest over alleged mistreatment
stories.summary: Inmates at a Venezuelan prison have occupied the roof and set fires to protest conditions they say involve abuse and shootings by guards. The clashes between prisoners and authorities reflect broader concerns about treatment within the country's detention system.

stories.headline: Gaza flotilla activists return to Australia, describing abuse
stories.summary: Australian activists from a Gaza-bound flotilla have returned home and reported experiencing sexual assault, beatings, and torture during their detention by Israeli forces. Their accounts have prompted Malaysia to consider bringing Israel before the International Court of Justice, while Arab and Muslim states have issued formal condemnations.
